transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been experiencing some really confusing changes in my thinking and how I speak for about a year and nine months now. My thoughts just feel very jumbled up, and it's making it really hard to communicate with people. I just want to figure out why my mind is acting this way.
Along with these changes in your thinking, have you also experienced long periods of feeling very down and depressed, or times when you felt unusually high and energetic?
No, I haven't really experienced those kinds of extreme mood changes. My mood has been pretty much the same, so I'm not sure about feeling really high or low.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ['Schizophrenia', 'Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)', 'Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)', 'Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features', 'Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features']. Based on this conversation, the patient denies experiencing any periods of mania, hypomania, or severe depression during the 21 months of their cognitive and speech symptoms. This rules out Schizoaffective Disorder (both Bipolar and Depressive types), Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features, and Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features, leaving Schizophrenia as the primary candidate.
